scope: Desktop right inspector history/attachment tab flicker
root_cause: The transition retained the previous view only when its tab matched the requested tab. Changing tabs therefore removed the complete list before the incoming metadata arrived.
changes: Retain the current complete view during a tab read, using the existing atomic handoff when the incoming list is ready.
Commit tab selection, keyboard tab stop and tabpanel labelling with the displayed list so that retained history is never labelled as attachments or vice versa.
Keep retained content inert, close attachment previews and remask expanded history immediately while waiting for the next active view.
Keep fresh metadata reads, descending order, independent scroll, error/retry behavior and stale object/account/session response rejection; do not add a shared data cache.

validation.before_fix: All 4 new controlled tab-handoff regression cases failed against the original implementation; 10 unrelated cases were intentionally excluded from this reproduction.
validation.unit_tests: 53 passed across ObjectInspectorPanel, HistoryViewer and editor field-suggestion handoff (3 files), including the 4 new tab cases.

production_browser.broad_run: 29 passed; 5 test-assumption failures: four new cases assumed the attachment page size for history, and one existing case checked immediate unmount before asynchronous handoff completed.
production_browser.targeted_recheck: 8 passed with no retries after correcting those assertions: 4 tab-handoff cases and all 4 long-name scrolling cases. The application implementation was unchanged between the broad run and this recheck.
production_browser.preservation: Rapid tab reversal, an object switch during a pending tab read, stale response rejection, protected history remasking, stable panel/scroll nodes, descending lists and no page errors passed.

validation.targeted_eslint: passed, including the final browser test changes
validation.native_acceptance: No new Windows or macOS native executable acceptance was performed; production browser platform fixtures were used.

delivery: One independent fix committed and pushed directly on main, without a feature branch or pull request.
